questions.title: Insert into Sorted List
questions.description:
A leaderboard list is kept in ascending order. Insert the new value so the list STAYS ascending: allocate the node, find the first node whose successor is bigger (or the tail), and splice it in. Return the head. std::sort / stable_sort are banned — the list is already ascending, just relink. The harness prints the resulting list space-separated. The program scaffolding (includes, the Node struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    Node* insert_sorted(Node* head, int value)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers in ascending order. Line 3: value.

Output Format:
One line with the resulting ascending list, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000, the list is ascending

questions.title: Detect Cycle with Floyd
questions.description:
A scheduler suspects a corrupted list loops back on itself. The harness builds the list and, when the extra input pos is 0-based p >= 0, links the tail to the node at index p (pos = -1 leaves the list open). Detect the cycle with Floyd's tortoise-and-hare: two pointers, the slow one stepping once and the fast one twice per round, meeting only if a cycle exists. Solve iteratively in O(1) extra memory — sets, maps, hash containers and vectors are banned. Report 1 if a cycle exists, else 0. The program scaffolding (includes, the Node struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int has_cycle(Node* head)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: pos (-1 = no link, else 0-based index < n).

Output Format:
One line: 1 if the list contains a cycle, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1 <= pos < n

questions.title: Delete Every Occurrence of Value
questions.description:
A spam filter purges a mailing chain: remove EVERY node whose data equals the given value, relinking the survivors so the remaining order is preserved. The tests always leave at least one survivor. std::remove is banned — relink the nodes yourself (a dummy head node keeps the front case simple). Return the new head; the harness prints the resulting list space-separated. The program scaffolding (includes, the Node struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    Node* delete_all(Node* head, int value)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: value.

Output Format:
One line with the surviving values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000, at least one node survives

questions.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
questions.description:
A metrics pipeline receives two ASCENDING lists and must produce one ascending list by SPLICING the existing nodes in a single pass (do not create new nodes and do not re-sort). Repeatedly link the smaller front node to the result tail until one list runs out, then link the rest. Return the merged head; the harness prints it space-separated. std::sort / stable_sort are banned. The program scaffolding (includes, the Node struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    Node* merge_sorted(Node* a, Node* b)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n ascending integers. Line 3: m. Line 4: m ascending integers.

Output Format:
One line with the merged ascending list, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000, both lists are ascending

questions.title: Palindrome Linked List Check
questions.description:
An audit tool checks whether a chain of ids reads the same forwards and backwards, WITHOUT extra memory: find the middle with slow/fast pointers, reverse the second half in place, compare the two halves node by node, and report 1 or 0. Copying the values into an array or vector is banned. (Reversing is allowed to scramble the list — the harness discards it afterwards.) The program scaffolding (includes, the Node struct and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int is_list_palindrome(Node* head)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: 1 if the list is a palindrome, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000
